A '''psychologist''' was an individual who specialized in the [[Medic/Legends|medical]] occupation of psychology. The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] had teams of psychologists,

==Description==
{{Quote|Some fancy doctor said we can switch on psychopathy.|Mandalorian Goran Beviin on the words of a psychologist|<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref>}}
Psychologists specialized in the psychological makeup of various [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="AE" /> They also specialized in a plethora of disorders such as [[multiple personality disorder]]<ref name="CRO">''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]''</ref> and [[psychopathy]].<ref name="Revelation" /> Some [[Medical droid/Legends|surgical droids]] were programmed to act as psychologists.<ref name="SWSB">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|In fact, [Cassio Tagge] is so rational that Alliance psychologists are in a fevered debate over what made him join in with the Empire in the first place.|The notes of Rebel [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]]|<ref name="GG1">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref>}}
During the [[Old Republic era]], [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] psychologists theorized that the [[Elomin/Legends|Elomin]] species' beliefs of other [[Species/Legends|species]] as inferior would make them ineffectual while traveling in [[Realspace/Legends|deep space]].<ref name="AE" /> While the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and the Old Republic raged on, psychologists made up a margin of the Republic's [[Belsavis prison]] personnel on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]].<ref name="Codex">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=codex|Belsavis Prison Personnel}}</ref>

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] had a plethora of psychologists at hand.<ref name="RASB" /> Due to the destruction of his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] [[Bront]] and the [[Death/Legends|death]] of his family, Rebel operative [[Graf Yonna]] suffered a mental break and created an [[Multiple personality disorder|alternate personality]] based on hero and adventurer [[Parsol d'Ahndole]]. Rebel psychologists tried to reconstruct his original personality.<ref name="CRO" /> The [[Interrogation (Alliance Intelligence)|Interrogation]] department of [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] employed psychologists who used psychic interrogation techniques to persuade captured [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperials]] to talk.<ref name="RASB" /> Alliance psychologists were perplexed as to why [[General/Legends|General]] [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]] of the Empire had decided to serve [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], given he was the most rational and stable amongst the generals stationed aboard the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]].<ref name="GG1" />

A psychologist once said that the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warriors had the ability to "switch off" [[psychopathy]]. In [[41 ABY]],<ref name="Rev Date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]'', including the conversation between Beviin and Solo, to [[41 ABY]].</ref> Mandalorian [[Goran Beviin]] told [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] about this saying.<ref name="Revelation" />

==Behind the scenes==
Psychologists were first mentioned in ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'', written by [[Bill Slavicsek]] and [[Curtis Smith]] in [[1987]] as the first rulebook in [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="SWSB" /> Psychologists first appeared in the form of the "Mon Calamari Mediator" player character template in the ''[[Death in the Undercity]]'' adventure for [[West End Games]]' [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]], written by [[Michael Nystul]] and published in [[1990]].<ref name="DITU">''[[Death in the Undercity]]''</ref>
